title: jobs.json (all jobs + their full embedded host grids) is rewritten twice per job execution just to flip the RunningState marker
existing_state: Each JobDefinition embeds a complete snapshot of its host grid (Hosts + HostColumns, Models/JobDefinition.cs:159-164) — deliberate, so jobs are immune to grid edits. But the crash-recovery marker RunningState also lives on JobDefinition (219-223, doc: persisted to jobs.json while executing), and JobStorageService has only whole-file persistence: PersistToDisk serializes every job and does a full .bak copy first (Services/JobStorageService.cs:227-244). JobExecutionService sets job.RunningState and calls _jobStorage.Save(job) at every run start (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:768-774) and clears it at every completion (827-832) — so one scheduled run = two full rewrites + two full .bak copies of a file whose size is dominated by every job's host snapshot. With several fleet-sized jobs on minute-level cron schedules, that is continuous multi-MB write amplification for a one-field change, all to a single contended file (and each Save also fires JobsChanged, amplifying the Job List dialog refresh storm).
recommendation: Move the in-flight marker out of the monolith: persist running-state to a tiny sidecar (e.g. running-jobs.json mapping jobId -> StartedUtc) written atomically via JsonFileWriter.WriteJsonAtomic, and have the startup crash-recovery scan read that sidecar instead of JobDefinition.RunningState (keep deserializing the old field for one release to migrate). jobs.json then only changes when a job definition actually changes. Alternatively (bigger): per-job definition files under a jobs/ directory so any save touches only the affected job.
user_benefit: Stops the scheduler from hammering the disk proportionally to fleet size on every single run, and removes the risk window where a crash mid-rewrite of the whole jobs file is in play twice per execution.

evidence.note: embedded host snapshot per job; RunningState persisted to jobs.json while executing
_jobStorage.Save(job) on every run start and completion
PersistToDisk: .bak File.Copy + serialize ALL jobs + File.WriteAllText on every Save
